definitions.explanation: A serious dramatic work with an unhappy ending, typically involving the downfall of the main character.
A very sad, unfortunate, or disastrous event or situation.

examples.english: We must not repeat this tragedy.

notes:
USAGE: {悲劇|ひげき} refers to both the dramatic genre (tragedy) and real-world tragic events.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{悲劇|ひげき}を⟦{生|う}む→産む：01899_umu⟧ (to create tragedy)
・{悲劇|ひげき}を⟦{繰|く}り{返|かえ}す→繰り返す：02051_kurikaesu⟧ (to repeat tragedy)
・{悲劇|ひげき}に⟦{見舞|みま}われる→見舞われる：27351_mimawareru⟧ (to be struck by tragedy)
・⟦{悲劇|ひげき}{的|てき}→悲劇的：28215_higekiteki⟧ (tragic)

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
・⟦{悲劇|ひげき}{的|てき}→悲劇的：28215_higekiteki⟧ (tragic - adjective)
・{悲劇|ひげき}⟦{俳優|はいゆう}→俳優：03547_haiyuu⟧ (tragic actor)
・{四大|しだい}{悲劇|ひげき} (four great tragedies - Shakespeare)

ANTONYM:
・⟦{喜劇|きげき}→喜劇：11835_kigeki⟧ (comedy)

LITERARY NOTE: The four great tragedies of Shakespeare (ハムレット, オセロ, リア{王|おう}, マクベス) are called {四大|しだい}{悲劇|ひげき} in Japanese.
